newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tanks holding 38,600 tonnes crude seen damaged.
newsitem.headline: Tanks holding 38,600 tonnes crude seen damaged.

text.p: Two storage compartments filled with 38,600 tonnes of crude oil appear to have been damaged when a supertanker scraped a reef in shallow waters of Tokyo bay and spilled oil on Wednesday morning, said the tanker's operator Nippon Yusen KK.
A third compartment filled with water was also damaged in the incident, a Nippon Yusen spokesman said.

It was unclear how much crude oil had spilled into the bay, a Nippon Yusen spokesman said, but he added that it was unlikely the total volume in the two damaged tanks had leaked, judging from television footage of the spill.
The Japanese coastguard said it was likely the single-hulled tanker may have leaked 11,000 tonnes of crude oil, which would make it one of Japan's biggest oil spills.
The 259,999 deadweight tonne Panamanian-flagged Diamond Grace was on its way to Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd's Kawasaki refinery, carrying 257,000 tonnes of crude from the United Arab Emirates.
The Maritime Safety Agency said it was not yet clear whether the flow of oil from the tanker had stopped.
